articles.title: Rohit Sharma's 5th T20I century and two super overs: A look at what happened when India last played in Bengaluru as IND vs WI set for series decider at Chinnaswamy
articles.summary: Shai Hope struck another century as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth Twenty20 in Hyderabad on Wednesday to level the five-match series at
articles.body: Shai Hope struck another century as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth Twenty20 in Hyderabad on Wednesday to level the five-match series at 2-2.Chasing 248, India got off to a quick start, with Sanju Samson reaching his half-century in just 20 balls before Keemo Paul dismissed him for 56.Shreyas Iyer added 16 off 11 balls, while Abhishek Sharma scored 29 before Gudakesh Motie sent the opener back. India mounted another push towards the end through Nitish Kumar Reddy and Tilak Varma, who put together 70 runs off just 32 balls to keep the chase alive.Varma was dismissed for 43, while Paul removed Reddy and took two more wickets in the 19th over, bringing India's chase to a halt. The lower order could not offer much resistance as India were bowled out for 223.Bengaluru will host the series-deciding T20I on Saturday.What happened when India last played a T20I in BengaluruIndia last played a T20I in Bengaluru on January 17, 2024, when they faced Afghanistan in the third and final match of the series. India had already secured the series by winning the first two games.But the final match was far from a dead rubber. It produced a series of dramatic moments, including two Super Overs and a controversial episode involving Rohit Sharma.In the first Super Over, Afghanistan's Mohammad Nabi and Rahmanullah Gurbaz ran extra runs after the ball deflected off Nabi's body on the final delivery. The incident left Virat Kohli angry, with the India batter seen clapping in Nabi's face.The drama continued moments later. With two runs needed off the final ball of first super over, Rohit, who was at the non-striker's end, walked off to allow Rinku Singh to take over the running. However, Yashasvi Jaiswal's bottom edge went straight to the wicketkeeper, and India could manage only a single, leaving the first Super Over tied.Rohit was ready to bat again in the second Super Over. Under point 22 of Appendix F of the playing conditions, a batter who had retired could return only if the retirement had been due to injury, illness or "any other unavoidable cause".Earlier in the match, Rohit had won the toss and elected to bat. India suffered a disastrous start, losing four wickets inside the powerplay. Jaiswal fell at 18 in the third over, Kohli was dismissed at the same score in the fourth, Shivam Dube departed at 21, and India lost their fourth wicket at 22.Rohit kept the innings together and combined with Rinku for a 190-run partnership for the fifth wicket. India recovered from 22/4 to finish at 212/4, with Rohit scoring 121 off 69 balls and Rinku making 69 off 38 deliveries.Rohit became the first batter to score five centuries in T20 internationals, rescuing India from a position where they had lost four wickets for just 22 runs.Afghanistan matched India's total, forcing the match into a Super Over. Gulbadin Naib led their fightback with 55 off 23 balls.Naib and Gurbaz came out to bat in the first Super Over, which was bowled by Mukesh Kumar. A mix-up between the batters resulted in Naib being run out. Gurbaz and Nabi then scored runs before the controversial final delivery.The batters ran a bye, but the throw from wicketkeeper Sanju Samson deflected off Nabi's leg towards long-on. The pair ran two more runs. Rohit and his teammates were unhappy with the outcome, though the running was within the rules.India needed 17 runs to win the first Super Over. Rohit hit Azmatullah Omarzai for two successive sixes to leave India needing three runs off the final two balls. With two runs required from the last delivery, Rohit retired hurt to allow Rinku, the quicker runner, to take over. But Jaiswal could only edge the ball towards the wicketkeeper, and India managed just one run, leaving the Super Over tied.India clinch the second Super OverBy the time the second Super Over began, Rohit had already spent a long time at the crease. He nevertheless hit Fareed Ahmad for a six and a four to give India a strong start. Rinku was dismissed off the first ball, however, and Samson then ran Rohit out, leaving Afghanistan with a target of 12.India handed the ball to leg-spinner Ravi Bishnoi, and he delivered under pressure. Nabi flat-batted a short delivery straight to the fielder at long-off on the first ball, while Gurbaz fell on the third delivery after attempting a similar shot.India won the second Super Over to seal the match after one of the most eventful finishes in T20I cricket.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Kuwait's success in the Sub-Regional Asia A Qualifier for the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2028 in Malaysia has highlighted the role played by the ILT20 in
articles.body: Kuwait's success in the Sub-Regional Asia A Qualifier for the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2028 in Malaysia has highlighted the role played by the ILT20 in preparing players from the country for international cricket.Several members of Kuwait's qualifying team have featured in the ILT20, where they have trained and played alongside international stars. They believe the experience has helped them improve their game and prepare for the international stage.Bilal Tahir, who scored 16 off seven balls against Bahrain and remained unbeaten on 32 off 16 balls against Qatar during the qualifier, said his time with the Desert Vipers helped him understand what it takes to be part of a title-winning team."Winning the title with the Desert Vipers showed me what a championship environment looks like. Seeing how players like Sam Curran, Fakhar Zaman and Lockie Ferguson train and prepare every day raised my own standards, and I have tried to hold myself to that level ever since. I hope many more players from Kuwait get the chance to experience the ILT20, because it can transform a cricketer’s career."Mohamed Shafeeq, who became the first Kuwait player to feature in a ILT20 match when he represented MI Emirates last season, said sharing a dressing room with experienced international players helped him understand the tactical side of T20 cricket."Walking out for MI Emirates for the first time was a moment I will never forget, it was special for me and for cricket in Kuwait. Sharing a dressing room with players like Kieron Pollard and Shakib Al Hasan, you learn how much thought goes into every situation in a T20 game, and that changes the way you approach your own cricket.I have tried to bring that understanding back to the Kuwait team and share what I have learned. I am really looking forward to returning to MI Emirates for Season 5 and continuing to learn."Kuwait players also featured among the leading wicket-takers in the qualifier. Mohamed Aslam finished second on the list with 15 wickets in six innings, while Adnan Idrees took 12 wickets in six innings to finish third. Both played in Season 4 of the ILT20, with Idrees also named Player of the Tournament.Kuwait's representation in the league will continue in Season 5, with Ravija Sandaruwan set to join Abu Dhabi Knight Riders. Sandaruwan finished as the qualifier's third-highest run-scorer, making 176 runs in six innings."I am very excited to be joining the Abu Dhabi Knight Riders for ILT20 Season 5. I have seen how much my teammates grew from their time in the league last season, and I want to make the most of the same opportunity.The Qualifier gave me a lot of confidence with the bat, and I want to carry that form into the season. Playing alongside and against world-class cricketers is the best way to test yourself, and I hope to learn as much as I can and bring that experience back to the Kuwait team."Five other Kuwait players will also feature in Season 5. articles.title: Punam Raut, part of India's 2017 World Cup final run, retires from international cricket
articles.summary: Out-of-favour India women's cricket team top-order batter Punam Raut on Thursday announced her retirement from all forms of international cricket with
articles.body: Out-of-favour India women's cricket team top-order batter Punam Raut on Thursday announced her retirement from all forms of international cricket with immediate effect.The 37-year-old represented India in four Tests, 73 ODIs and 35 T20Is between 2009 and 2021.“After much thought and reflection, I have decided to retire from international cricket in all formats of the game,” Raut said in a post on her Instagram page."Representing India has been the greatest honour of my life. Cricket has been more than just a sport — it has shaped my character, taught me resilience, and given me memories that I will cherish forever. Every time I wore the India jersey, I did so with immense pride and gratitude.“Wearing the India jersey was a dream that became a reality, and I will always be grateful for the trust and support I received.”Raut also thanked the Mumbai Cricket Association for its role in her development as a cricketer.“My sincere thanks to the Mumbai Cricket Association for believing in me during my formative years. The opportunities and guidance I received there laid the foundation of my cricketing journey,” Raut said.She scored 2,299 runs in 73 ODIs, 719 runs in 35 T20Is and 264 runs in four Tests. Her international career included four centuries — three in ODIs and one in a Test against South Africa in 2014 — along with 15 ODI half-centuries and four in T20Is. Her last international appearance was in an ODI against England in June 2021.One of Raut's most memorable performances came during India's run to the 2017 Women's World Cup final. She scored 381 runs in the tournament, including 86 against England in the final at Lord's, which India lost by nine runs.During the same World Cup, Raut scored 109 against Ireland and shared a record 320-run opening partnership with Deepti Sharma.In 2021, Raut was part of India's historic pink-ball Test against Australia. She scored 36 in the first innings and earned praise for walking off after edging a delivery despite being given not out.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Former India spinner R Ashwin has criticised the team management for dropping Kuldeep Yadav during the ongoing T20I series against the West Indies,
articles.body: Former India spinner R Ashwin has criticised the team management for dropping Kuldeep Yadav during the ongoing T20I series against the West Indies, questioning the decision to leave out a wrist-spinner who had troubled the visiting batters.Kuldeep featured in the first two matches in Lucknow and Ranchi before being left out of the playing XI for the games in Indore and Hyderabad. He returned figures of 2/33 in the opening T20I but conceded 53 runs in the second match, which India went on to lose.India’s bowling concerns persisted in the fourth T20I in Hyderabad, where the West Indies piled up 247 runs in 20 overs and secured a 24-run victory. Reacting to Kuldeep’s omission, Ashwin said he could not understand why the team management had seemingly lost confidence in the spinner.“It is very surprising because, on a ground where you expect to get some bounce, I know it has not always been a happy hunting ground for spinners, but the West Indies batters are struggling to pick his googly and leg-spin,” Ashwin said on his YouTube channel.He questioned the logic behind excluding Kuldeep against an opposition that had found it difficult to read his variations, adding, “So, if you are leaving Kuldeep out against them, it lacks a bit of common sense.”Ashwin also emphasised the potential impact of Kuldeep’s presence, suggesting that the spinner could have helped restrict the West Indies’ total. “It is very surprising because I think his presence could have made a difference of 15-20 runs,” he said.'I was surprised': AshwinWhile Ashwin acknowledged that leaving Kuldeep out in Indore was understandable given the ground’s small dimensions, he rejected the suggestion that the spinner’s performance was responsible for India’s defeat in Ranchi.“I was surprised. Kuldeep was not picked in Indore, and I would still endorse that decision because I can understand that the ground is small,” Ashwin explained.However, he disagreed with attributing the Ranchi defeat to Kuldeep, stating, “But you are almost making an issue out of it by suggesting that India’s loss in Ranchi was because of Kuldeep. articles.title: ‘Series in India brings nothing to West Indies’: Cricket’s bilateral revenue model sparks debate
articles.summary: Cricket West Indies (CWI) CEO Chris Dehring has questioned the financial system governing bilateral cricket, explaining how it has contributed to the
articles.body: Cricket West Indies (CWI) CEO Chris Dehring has questioned the financial system governing bilateral cricket, explaining how it has contributed to the board’s ongoing financial difficulties. Despite the West Indies currently playing a T20I series against India, Dehring said the Caribbean board would not receive any revenue from the series, even as the hosts stand to earn millions.The T20I series is level at 2-2 following Shai Hope’s century in Hyderabad. Speaking to The Scoop by Wisden Cricket, Dehring explained that the financial model leaves visiting teams without a share of the broadcasting revenue generated by bilateral matches."West Indies cricket receives nothing in this case, because the series is being played in India," said Dehring. "A series that could generate $20 million to $30 million in India brings West Indies cricket no revenue."How the revenue system changedDehring traced the problem back to 1997, when nine of the 10 ICC member countries voted to change cricket’s financial model. Before that decision, host nations generally paid visiting teams a guaranteed fee, which sometimes earned the West Indies more than hosting matches at home."To understand how this happened, you have to go back to 1997," he added. "I was fortunate, or unfortunate, to be around when the ICC member countries voted to change the financial model that underpinned world cricket. Until then, West Indies was a very attractive team, and everybody wanted us to tour. We would receive a touring fee, which was often worth more than we could earn by hosting a series in the Caribbean."Under the revised system, the country hosting a bilateral series could retain all the revenue generated from its broadcasting rights. Dehring argued that this created a major imbalance between countries with large audiences and smaller cricketing nations."That meant India could retain the revenues generated by a population of one and a half billion people, while West Indies could retain whatever revenues we could generate in Antigua, with its population of around 100,000, or St Kitts, with around 30,000," Dehring continued."It was palpably unfair. We were outvoted nine to one by the ICC member countries. At the time, I said that this decision had effectively signed the demise of West Indies cricket because it took away our main source of income," he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India’s No. 8 obsession: Why Kuldeep Yadav is caught in the crossfire
articles.summary: Over the last 15 months, the No.
articles.body: Over the last 15 months, the No. 8 spot in the batting line-up has been a sensitive topic of discussion whenever the Indian team management has sat down to finalise the playing XI. It is a position that has consumed the most mind space and yielded the bare minimum returns.Whether it is picking Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shardul Thakur in Tests, or accommodating a spin-bowling all-rounder in Washington Sundar, or more recently Naman Dhir, in white-ball cricket, these resources have invariably been underused.For instance, Dhir was parachuted into the playing XI during West Indies’ ongoing white-ball tour of India. He has earned his stripes as a batter, but both Shubman Gill in ODIs and Shreyas Iyer in T20Is have primarily used him for his off-spinning abilities. While he has looked like a spinner who can effectively chip in to make up for the fifth bowler, the true purpose of his inclusion is yet to be established.In this scenario, Kuldeep Yadav has found himself caught in the crossfire. After the end of the ODI series, Gill was blunt in his admission that the team management was willing to try as many options as possible to find someone who could bat and bowl at No. 8.He categorically mentioned that Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi would remain in the mix because of their batting skills. The fact is that the No. 8 batter has barely managed to make any impact with the ball. And by the time the No. 8 comes out to bat, he has very little room to alter the course of the game.Yet, it appears that the team management is obsessed with the idea that the balance of the XI depends on the player who bats at No. 8.The majority of the matches India have lost during this period have been because of the excessive burden on the batters to put up a score well beyond par in the prevailing conditions. The question that arises here is whether India should consider bringing in a specialist attacking bowler who could restrict the opposition to a lower score, especially on the batting-friendly pitches at home.India’s problems stem from the fact that the team does not have a genuine all-rounder besides the injury-prone Hardik Pandya, who can be equally effective with the ball as the third seamer in white-ball cricket and as a batter who can comfortably be sent in to bat in the middle order.Pandya’s back-up project, Reddy, has shown flashes of promise as a lower-order finisher, but his bowling cannot make up for the absence of a third seamer. It is an irony that a position traditionally meant for a specialist bowler is now being decided on the basis of batting skills.India enjoyed a potent pace-bowling attack until the 2023 World Cup, complemented by established spinners. Gill did not fail to mention how much that makes a difference to a line-up. Evidently, India’s white-ball set-up does not have that luxury at the moment.While the next marquee T20 assignment is two years away, the team management does not have much time to find the right combination before next year’s ODI World Cup in Africa.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s recent performances have proved that class and skill can endure. He can enjoy his time in the Indian jersey ... articles.summary: Former India batter Wasim Jaffer believes Rinku Singh’s absence is hurting India in the ongoing T20I series against the West Indies, arguing that the
articles.body: Former India batter Wasim Jaffer believes Rinku Singh’s absence is hurting India in the ongoing T20I series against the West Indies, arguing that the left-hander could have made a difference in the fourth match.India suffered a 24-run defeat on Wednesday after the visitors successfully defended a target of 248 to level the five-match series at 2-2. Shai Hope led the charge with an unbeaten 102 off 50 balls as the West Indies finished at 247/3. India, in reply, were bowled out for 223 in 19.3 overs, with Arshdeep Singh retiring hurt in the final over as the chase came to an end.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Jaffer questioned the decision to leave Rinku out of the Indian side, insisting that the batter's ability to deliver in the middle and lower order makes him a valuable option."If you look from a batter's perspective, Rinku is miles ahead of everyone else. He bats amazingly at number five and six, plus he is a left-hander. I feel it is very unfortunate that he is not part of this Indian team purely because he cannot bowl. I can understand Rajat's (Patidar) case, as he bats in the top order and there is no place there, but Rinku should be there," Jaffer said.The former India batter felt Rinku could have given India a chance to turn the game around during the fourth T20I, pointing to the finisher's record in franchise cricket."If you had Rinku in that position, you never know. He could have changed the game. He has the capacity and has won a lot of matches in franchise cricket in this manner," he added.Rinku has struggled to secure a regular place in India's playing XI and was eventually left out of the squad after the Zimbabwe tour. His numbers this year have been modest, with 152 runs from 13 matches at an average of 25.33 and a strike rate of 139.44. His highest score in that period is 44 not out.However, his record when batting at No. 5 or 6 in T20Is tells a different story. In 22 innings in those positions, Rinku has scored 518 runs at an average of 43.15 and a strike rate of 156.00, underlining his effectiveness in the role Jaffer believes he should be given.Jaffer also assessed India's decision to include Naman Dhir in the T20I side, expressing reservations about expecting the all-rounder to bowl his full quota of four overs. He said off-spinners can struggle outside the powerplay when they lack variations, particularly on Indian pitches."It is a bit difficult for off-spinners to bowl after the powerplay if you don't have variety. Roston Chase does it; credit to him. If you do not have that cleverness or variation, especially in India, it becomes very difficult. So to expect that Naman Dhir will bowl four overs is too ambitious," he said.Jaffer added that Dhir's contribution with the bat would be crucial to his place in the T20I side. The all-rounder has managed just 14 runs across three innings in the series, but Jaffer believes he has the ability to provide a quick contribution."I feel his performance with the bat is very important for him to play T20 cricket. Unfortunately, that has not happened in the last two matches, but he has the capability to come and play a quick 25-30 cameo," he signed off.With the series tied at 2-2, India and the West Indies will face off in the fifth and final T20I in Bengaluru on Saturday, October 17.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mason Crane 'buzzing' at England recall as Glamorgan leg-spinner credits Richard Dawson with turnaround in fortunes
articles.summary: Mason Crane tells the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast: "I don't want to just be a highlights reel bowler"; watch England's first game of ODI tri-series in Pakistan on Tuesday, against the hosts, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8.30am (play starts 9am)
articles.body:
Crane was capped three times as a 20-year-old, nine years ago, the last of which was his Test debut in the final match of England's 2017/18 Ashes tour in Sydney. He'd take a single wicket as the tourists signed off a 4-0 series drubbing with another defeat.

Speaking to the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast , Crane admitted that he was "resigned to the fact it may not come again" as a near decade passed without further recognition, until getting the call for England's upcoming ODI tri-series in Pakistan.

"I didn't really expect it, to be honest," Crane said. "It was a bit out of the blue. But it's really cool and I'm buzzing.

"I think there was a period a few years ago where I was sort of resigned to the fact it may not come again, where I maybe put a bit too much pressure on myself and wasn't particularly enjoying it.

"But the last couple of years I feel like I've I sort of got that spark back and the ambition that comes with it."

Following his initial England breakthrough in 2017, injuries ruined Crane's 2018 season and he struggled to nail down a regular spot for his county Hampshire, until a 2024 move to Glamorgan prompted a change in fortunes.

There, he thrived under the coaching of Richard Dawson, who has just left to join England's red-ball staff as assistant to the newly-appointed Stephen Fleming.

"Daws is a brilliant coach. He's been absolutely amazing for us," Crane said. "He has very high standards; he pushes you to become the best version of yourself, and we all sort of thrived off that.

"From a Glamorgan point of view, we'd obviously rather have kept him. But when you have someone like Daws as your coach, if we're if we're being brutally honest, I think you know at some point that he's going to go on to international cricket.

"He's such a brilliant manager of people. He'll be amazing in any role he does.

"It's amazing for England. And like I said, I'm sure one day he will be in a position to take over an international side. He's that kind of calibre of coach."

Crane on batting form - 'My confidence just grew and grew'

Crane's return to the England fold has as much to do with his hugely-improved form with the bat, as much as his performances with the ball.

Crane struck a maiden first-class century, swiftly following with a second, as Glamorgan finished safely in sixth place upon their first County Championship season in Division One since 2005.

"I've always believed I underperformed a bit with the bat," Crane said. "When I moved to Glamorgan and started playing a lot more regularly, I kind of realised I had a few more shots.

"My confidence just grew and grew. And then this year, to get a few big scores has been amazing.

"Ironically, that's helped my bowling because I'm now bowling in matches where I probably wouldn't be playing in to start with."

Crane claimed 34 wickets across 14 County Championship appearances in 2026, and 15 in 10 Vitality Blast outings. He also played three times for London Spirit in The Hundred, taking two wickets.

A couple of his dismissals went viral on social media, particularly those of Yorkshire batters George Hill and James Wharton as part of an eight-wicket match haul back in April, but Crane doesn't want to just be Insta-famous.

"I don't want to just be a highlights reel bowler, every now and then bowl a really good ball and just live off that," he added.

"I pride myself on trying to play to the situations really, trying to work out how I'm going to get the most out of a wicket and get a particular guy out.

"I've also given myself a bit more freedom, I guess, with the ball now. I try and bowl more variations, but I'm also better at bowling them now.

"It's about sort of adding as many strings to your bow. It's really important."

articles.body: Former India batter Mohammad Kaif has questioned India’s team combination after Shreyas Iyer and his side suffered a 24-run defeat to West Indies in the fourth T20I in Hyderabad, arguing that the management prioritised batting depth over a stronger bowling attack.India entered the contest with four specialist bowlers and two all-rounders, but the combination failed to contain the West Indies batters, who piled up 247/3 in their 20 overs. The hosts responded with an aggressive batting effort but could manage only 223 before being bowled out, allowing the visitors to level the five-match series 2-2.Kaif felt India’s selection was not suited to the conditions and said the team needed to rely on specialist bowlers rather than expect its batting line-up to compensate for a lack of bowling options."Having batting till No.8 is not bravery. Bravery is playing your proper bowlers on a good batting wicket. A brave call is one where you pick seven batters and five proper bowlers, including Axar Patel as the all-rounder. Bravery is not allowing the opposition to score 250 and then saying we'll chase it down. If you actually play with five main bowlers, you won't need to chase so many. The flatter the conditions, the more specialist bowlers should play," Kaif said on Cricbuzz.India’s difficulties with the ball have been evident across the series. They were unable to defend a target of 250 in the second T20I, while they conceded 209 in the third match despite securing a 14-run win. articles.title: Jaguars’ Parker Washington has humbled reaction to Tom Brady’s praise
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington has continued to be a revelation, helping the team to a promising 4-1 start, including a three-game win...
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington has continued to be a revelation , helping the team to a promising 4-1 start, including a three-game winning streak.

"This guy's transformed from a fun story into an absolute dog. D-A-W-G. Everyone knows the sixth round, that's where you look when you need talent, right? Come get it," said Brady.

articles.title: ‘We want batters till No. 8’: Chahal reveals Rohit Sharma’s message before World Cup snub
articles.summary: Yuzvendra Chahal was among India’s most successful white-ball spinners, but his international career took a turn in 2023 when he was left out of the squad
articles.body: Yuzvendra Chahal was among India’s most successful white-ball spinners, but his international career took a turn in 2023 when he was left out of the squad for the ODI World Cup at home. Despite his reputation as an attacking leg-spinner and an impressive record in T20Is, Chahal did not feature in a single match at the 2024 T20 World Cup either.The 36-year-old, who last played an ODI in January 2023, has now opened up about missing out on India’s 15-member squad for the 2023 World Cup. Speaking to former India opener Aakash Chopra, Chahal revealed that then-captain Rohit Sharma had personally explained the team management’s thinking behind the decision.According to Chahal, India wanted to strengthen their batting depth and retain the option of playing an additional fast bowler, leaving little room for him in the team’s plans.“In 2023, when I went to play County, Rohit had told me that we want batters till number eight, so we were going with that. He told me clearly that they were also looking for an extra fast bowler for the World Cup. So it was made clear to me. After the World Cup, I just stopped thinking about selection,” Chahal said.The leg-spinner last represented India in a T20I in August 2023, but was picked for the 2024 T20 World Cup following an impressive IPL season. However, he remained on the sidelines throughout the tournament.Chahal said he approached the 2024 IPL without putting himself under additional pressure, focusing instead on enjoying his cricket. His performances caught Rohit’s attention, with the former India captain indicating that he wanted him in the World Cup squad.“In the IPL 2024, I just came to enjoy and did not put extra pressure on myself. That season, I did well, and Rohit told me he wanted me and we would see in the selection meeting,” he added.Chahal made his T20I debut in mid-2016 and went on to claim 96 wickets in 78 matches, establishing himself among India’s leading wicket-takers in the format.Asked which omission affected him the most, Chahal said missing out on the squad altogether was more difficult to accept than being selected but not getting a game. He explained that being part of the team at the 2022 tournament at least gave him clarity about his role and the circumstances in which he might play.“I felt worse in 2021 because I was not there at all. In 2022, at least I was in the team. Sometimes you also know the combination may not work. So I did not think a lot. But you always feel that you should have at least played one World Cup game. Rohit had told me that I would play only if a particular combination worked. So at least I had the clarity,” he said.Away from international cricket, Chahal recently completed a County stint with Northamptonshire in August before announcing his retirement from first-class cricket. He finished his first-class career with 148 wickets from 49 matches.Chahal, however, continues to be a major presence in the IPL. articles.title: ‘I was terrified’: Yuzvendra Chahal opens up on being hung from hotel balcony by ‘heavily drunk’ cricketer
articles.summary: Veteran India leg-spinner Yuzvendra Chahal has revisited a frightening episode from the early stages of his IPL career, revealing that an Australian
articles.body: Veteran India leg-spinner Yuzvendra Chahal has revisited a frightening episode from the early stages of his IPL career, revealing that an Australian cricketer, other than Andrew Symonds or James Franklin, was responsible for hanging him over a hotel balcony during the 2013 season.Chahal, the IPL’s leading wicket-taker with 233 scalps in 188 matches, began his career with Mumbai Indians in 2013 before going on to enjoy a successful eight-season stint with Royal Challengers Bengaluru.The incident first came to light in 2022, when Chahal disclosed that an intoxicated cricketer had dangled him upside down from a hotel balcony on the 15th floor. Speculation subsequently linked the episode to former Australia all-rounder Andrew Symonds.However, speaking on former India opener Aakash Chopra’s podcast, Chahal clarified that neither Symonds nor Franklin was involved. He recalled how the incident unfolded at a party hosted by RCB in Bengaluru, which he attended while representing Mumbai Indians."There was a party in Bengaluru hosted by RCB. I was playing for MI at the time. I also went there and saw a guy who was heavily drunk. He was well-built and very strong. He was from Australia, but he was neither Symonds nor Franklin, rather some other guy. He called me over and then lifted me into the air. At first, I thought he was joking, but then he hung me over the balcony, and I was just holding on to his neck," said Chahal.The leg-spinner said the situation quickly turned terrifying as the other cricketer continued to laugh while those present in the room watched in shock. He was eventually pulled back to safety after others stepped in."I was terrified. He was heavily drunk, and everyone in the room was stunned. Suddenly, everyone intervened and pulled me back up. That guy was laughing, but for me, it felt like a second birth. I think it was on the 15th or 16th floor of the hotel," he added.Chahal also acknowledged that his age and lack of experience at the time meant he did not know how to file a formal complaint over the incident. He eventually decided to put the episode behind him and concentrate on his cricket.The 36-year-old has since established himself as one of the most successful bowlers in IPL history, but his international career has stalled. His last appearance for India came in a T20I against the West Indies in 2023.Chahal currently plays for Punjab Kings in the IPL. During the 2026 season, he featured in 14 matches and took 12 wickets. articles.title: From Ravindra Jadeja’s century to Yashasvi Jaiswal’s duck: How India stars fared in Ranji Trophy
articles.summary: The BCCI’s decision to make domestic cricket participation mandatory for its players has brought several of India’s biggest names back into the Ranji
articles.body: The BCCI’s decision to make domestic cricket participation mandatory for its players has brought several of India’s biggest names back into the Ranji Trophy spotlight. Last season, Virat Kohli returned to Delhi’s red-ball side for the first time in 13 years, while Rohit Sharma turned out for Mumbai after a gap of nearly a decade.The trend has continued this season, with KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Ravindra Jadeja representing their respective state teams. With the opening round of matches now complete, the performances of some of India’s established internationals have offered a glimpse of where they stand ahead of upcoming assignments.KL Rahul: A rare failure for Karnataka batterAfter amassing 470 runs in four matches for Karnataka last season, Rahul endured a disappointing start to the new campaign. Playing against Andhra Pradesh, the opener managed just four runs in the first innings and one in the second.The twin failures came after Rahul had scored an ODI century against West Indies, making his early Ranji struggles a surprise. His decision to feature in domestic cricket could also help him prepare for India’s upcoming red-ball assignment in New Zealand, where windy conditions and a swinging ball are expected to pose a challenge.Rahul’s next outing will come in the three red-ball matches beginning October 24 in Lincoln, ahead of the two-Test series.Ravindra Jadeja: Hundred provides timely boostJadeja made the most of his opportunity with the bat for Saurashtra, registering his 16th first-class century with a score of 102. The all-rounder had not batted in a match since August 23 and had also missed out on an opportunity during India’s two ODIs against West Indies.While Jadeja’s days of hitting three triple-centuries in the 2011-12 season are long past, his latest hundred underlined that his appetite for big scores remains intact.His recent series in Sri Lanka had been relatively quiet with the bat, yielding scores of 43, 13 and nine, although he claimed eight wickets. With Jadeja expected to be part of India’s playing XI when the New Zealand Tests begin on November 19, the century could provide a valuable confidence boost.Yashasvi Jaiswal: Pressure builds after another setbackJaiswal’s preparations for the domestic season attracted attention even before the first ball was bowled, with the India opener practising wicketkeeping. His opening-round outing, however, proved brief, as he was dismissed for a 13-ball duck against Chandigarh in Mumbai’s innings victory.The left-hander has endured a mixed period despite scoring two centuries in his last three ODIs. He has been left out of the playing XI in the format, while his scores against Sri Lanka in August, 0, 32 and 45, offered little encouragement.For a batter regarded as one of India’s brightest prospects, the recent run has been challenging. However, Jaiswal is expected to feature in India’s XI for the New Zealand tour, which will be his first visit to the country with the national team. Reproducing the form he displayed in England last year could prove important in giving India a strong start.Mohammed Siraj: Hyderabad pacer looks to build rhythmSiraj’s place in India’s ODI plans is no longer assured, while workload management in Test cricket makes his opportunities in the format difficult to predict.The Hyderabad pacer turned out for his state side against Tripura and bowled nine overs in each innings. After failing to take a wicket in the first innings, he returned with figures of 2/19 in the second as Hyderabad dominated the opposition’s batting.It was a reasonable outing for Siraj, though more overs in the build-up to the New Zealand Tests could help him find greater rhythm and confidence.Mohammed Shami: Strong performance keeps India hopes aliveShami continued to make his case with an impressive display for Bengal against Delhi at Kalyani. The fast bowler claimed 4/30 in the first innings, helping dismiss Delhi for 240, before Bengal built a 229-run lead that proved crucial to the result.He was effective again in the second innings, taking 1/29 from 18 overs as Bengal secured a comprehensive victory.Shami has not represented India for more than a year with his last appeareacne coming in Champions Trophy 2025, and whether his domestic performances will earn him another national call-up remains uncertain. His latest outing, however, has once again raised the question of what more the experienced pacer needs to do to get back into contention.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Thomas Rew, 18, to captain England Lions against West Indies A
articles.summary: The elevation of teenager Thomas Rew to Lions captain is a further sign of the high regard he is held in by the England hierarchy and follows him being given his first senior call-up and central contract.
articles.body:
Teenager Thomas Rew has been named England Lions captain in the same week he earned his first senior call-up and central contract.

It is thought the 18-year-old will become the youngest captain in Lions history when he leads the side in three T20s against West Indies A in St Kitts and Nevis in November.

Rew skippers a squad that includes his older brother, James. Earlier this week, Thomas was given an England developmental deal and named in a full squad for the first time for the T20 series in Australia.

Thomas, Hampshire seamer Eddie Jack and Sussex all-rounder James Coles are the three players who will be involved on the Lions tour and then travel to Australia.

The Lions' T20s in the Caribbean are followed by five one-day matches, with the squad for that series captained by Test batter Dan Lawrence.

Lawrence is joined in the one-day squad by seamer Sam Cook, as both men use the Lions tour as part of their preparation for the senior team's three Tests in South Africa in December.

ECB abandons Rooney Rule for coach recruitment

The elevation of Thomas Rew to Lions captain is a further sign of the high regard he is held in by the England hierarchy.

The wicketkeeper-batter skippered England Under-19s to the final of the World Cup earlier this year, then made his first two first-class hundreds for Somerset during the summer.

Rew does not turn 19 until 29 November. If he plays on the senior tour of Australia, he would become the third-youngest man to make his England debut in any format after Rehan Ahmed and Brian Close, and the youngest man to play for England against Australia.

Hampshire seamer Scott Currie is also part of the T20 squad. Born in Poole, Currie played three one-day internationals for Scotland in 2014 and his brother Brad has 39 caps for the Scots.

Scott was called into England's squad for a T20 series in Ireland last year. Although he did not play, he was subsequently barred from reverting to Scotland at this year's T20 World Cup because he was named as an England substitute fielder in Dublin.

Former England batter Jonathan Trott is taking charge of the Lions' winter tours following the departure of former head coach Andrew Flintoff.

England Lions T20 squad for three-match T20 series v West Indies A: Thomas Rew (captain), Rehan Ahmed, Scott Currie, Adam Finch, Calvin Harrison, Jack Haynes, Eddie Jack, Ben Mayes, Ben McKinney, Liam Patterson-White, James Rew, Naavya Sharma, Ekansh Singh, Asa Tribe.

articles.title: 'Things got excessive after my divorce': Yuzvendra Chahal opens up on alcohol addiction
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Yuzvendra Chahal has opened up about his struggle with alcohol after his divorce, revealing that he checked into a rehabilitation centre for 26
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Yuzvendra Chahal has opened up about his struggle with alcohol after his divorce, revealing that he checked into a rehabilitation centre for 26 days to get his life back on track. The leg-spinner said his drinking had crossed limits and he realised that continuing on the same path could harm his cricket career.Chahal, who is the highest wicket-taker in IPL history with 233 wickets in 188 matches, spoke about his struggles in a podcast with former India opener Aakash Chopra.'Things got excessive after my divorce'Chopra asked Chahal when he decided to give up alcohol."After last year of county cricket. It crossed all limits, so I checked into a rehab centre and stayed there for 26 days. Now, I know how to handle it. That decision made a massive difference to my personal life. My maturity increased. My emotions are balanced now. Last IPL, my body felt like I was 30 years old again - doing gym work, fielding drills and training properly," Chahal said.When Chopra asked how his alcohol consumption began, Chahal said he was young when he started attending parties. He also recalled advice from former South Africa batter AB de Villiers."Initially, I was young. There were parties. In 2011, I played my first IPL. AB de Villiers once told me, 'Balance is key in life.' It sounds easy, but it is not. Things got excessive after my divorce, and my mental state was not that great," he said."I realised that if I continued down that path, I would ruin the very thing I love most - cricket. So I put an end to it, and now I am in a much happier and better space," Chahal said.Chahal's IPL recordDespite his personal struggles, Chahal has remained one of the leading wicket-takers in the IPL. He has taken 233 wickets in 188 matches, putting him at the top of the tournament's all-time list.He has also represented India in 72 ODIs, taking 121 wickets, and 80 T20Is, taking 96 wickets. articles.title: 'You take up this role to set a culture': Smriti Mandhana on the legacy she wants to leave as India captain
articles.summary: India's newly appointed captain Smriti Mandhana wants to improve the team's professionalism, power-hitting and fielding while building a strong team
articles.body: India's newly appointed captain Smriti Mandhana wants to improve the team's professionalism, power-hitting and fielding while building a strong team culture as India begin a new era with a three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe in Raipur on Friday.India will face Zimbabwe women's team for the first time in international cricket. The series will also give Mandhana a chance to begin preparing the team for the ICC Women's Champions Trophy 2027, which will be held in India."I have a job to do, I have to deliver. I always say this, that though the captain's name is first on the list, you're always the last on the list in terms of keeping everyone ahead," Mandhana said on JioStar's show 'Follow the Blues: The Dawn of Captain Smriti', as quoted by news agency PTI."I've been in the leadership group for a while now, but I definitely had written down a roadmap every time. The first thing which comes to my mind is the professionalism around it and trying to have this team go about things like a well-oiled machine."Like, taking our training, power-hitting, fielding and professionalism one notch higher. And, of course, setting a culture," she added.Mandhana, who takes over as captain as India build towards their next major international tournament, said she wants to establish standards that younger players can follow in the future."You always take up this role to leave it in a way where you set a culture for the team, for the rest of the girls to follow. So, you don't just do this for the sake of it," she said.The left-handed batter also spoke about the value of having former captain Harmanpreet Kaur in the dressing room, especially as several young players join the team."She's led India, she's the longest-serving captain, and has been such a great leader. So I'm sure that her experience, especially with a lot of youngsters coming into the team now, and the way she works towards the game, is going to be inspiring for a lot of people," Mandhana said."I hope they actually watch her, the way she goes about preparing for the game, and learn and take a lot of things from her."India have six T20I matches, including the three against Zimbabwe and three against South Africa, before the Champions Trophy, in addition to the Women's Premier League (WPL).Mandhana said the upcoming matches will help India decide how they want to play and which roles suit each player."It's going to be extremely important to see what style of cricket you want to play, what brand of cricket you want to play, and who's fitting where.
